items.title: 7 dead, officials suspended: What happened after the Satya Niketan building collapse?
items.summary: A five-storey building collapsed in Delhi’s Satya Niketan on Sunday afternoon. So far, 12 people have been pulled out from the debris, with seven deaths confirmed. Following the incident, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi has suspended its deputy commissioner, executive engineer, superintendent engineer, assistant engineer and junior engineer. Satya Niketan is home to a large number of Delhi University students, many of whom are forced to live in rented accommodation after failing to secure hostel rooms at their colleges. A local resident, Varun, said, “The entire building collapsed in one go. I think around 40 people could be trapped under the debris. Some repair work was going on here.” Police have registered a case and launched an investigation. The Delhi Fire Services said it received information about the collapse shortly after 1.30 pm. items.title: ANI files appeal before Delhi HC challenging denial of interim relief in case against OpenAI
items.summary: News agency Asian News International (ANI) has filed an appeal before the Delhi High Court against a single-judge's order denying it interim relief in its copyright infringement suit against OpenAI, the owner of ChatGPT. The appeal against the July 24 order is listed for hearing on September 8 before a Division Bench of Justices V Kameswaro Rao and Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora . ANI is the first Indian media house to sue OpenAI for copyright violation . Justice V Kameswar Rao and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora In its interim injunction application before the single-judge, the agency had sought directions to OpenAI to stop storing, publishing, reproducing or using ANI's copyrighted works. Several other publications had also joined ANI in its case, including the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA). The DNPA members include The Times Group, Hindustan Times, India Today Group, The Hindu and almost every major media house. However, the single-judge refused to pass such an order, holding that it would be against public interest. In his ruling, single-judge Justice Amit Bansal held that OpenAI's storage of news material published by ANI to train ChatGPT does not amount to copyright infringement. Notably, the single-judge said that irreparable injury would be caused not only to OpenAI but to public interest also if any interim injunction is granted in favour of ANI at this stage. The judge reasoned that ChatGPT has transformed information and is being used all around the world for beneficial purposes. ANI has now approached the division bench against the same. It is ANI's case that merely because its news content is publicly available, OpenAI does not get a right to exploit it or create copies of it to store. The news agency has said that in denying interim relief, the single-judge erred in the interpretation of the copyright law. Further, ANI has stated that the single judge's judgment expands the scope of fair use for commercial purposes beyond what is permitted by the Copyright Act Injunction against ChatGPT would hurt Indian AI development, users: Delhi HC differs with DPIIT white paper The appeal has been filed through advocate Sidhant Kumar of Unum Law.

A Division Bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev added that every time bureaucrats and those in the police ignore their oath and allegiance to India and its Constitution, people would view them as an oppressive vestige of the British Empire. Such a situation will arouse angst and hatred towards them and end up creating an environment of civil unrest in the State, the Bench added. It warned that if the Court fails to act against excesses of bureaucrats, the State may be reduced to an Orwellian Dystopia. "This Court, while correcting their excesses and/or illegalities, especially those that impinge upon the civil liberties of the citizens without adequate cause or due process (inhering in the procedure established by law), may pass harsh orders to compensate the citizen so wronged, besides recording their despotic conduct. Else, it shan't be long before the errant in the bureaucracy reduce the State of Uttar Pradesh to an Orwellian Dystopia," the Bench said. Justice S Vishwajith Shetty The case concerns alleged irregularities in the KPSC recruitment examination for 400 Veterinary Officer posts. The complaint alleged that relatives of KPSC officials secured unusually high marks, that some candidates were allegedly given access to the question paper before the examination, and that OMR sheets were tampered with. Middlemen allegedly approached candidates and promised to secure appointments for ₹70-80 lakhs, allegedly by manipulating their OMR marks. items.title: Supreme Court directs Centre, States to set up 449 exclusive NDPS courts within 6 months
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Central government, States, and Union Territories to take immediate steps to establish 449 exclusive courts for trial of cases under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS Act). A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued the directive after taking on record a status report filed by the Union of India, which revealed that only 176 of the required 449 exclusive NDPS courts are presently operational across the country. The Court expressed concern over the alarming surge in narcotics cases nationwide and directed setting up 449 courts, preferably within six months. “Having regard to the current pendency of cases under the NDPS Act and the alarming increase in offences under the Act across the country, it is expedient and in the interest of justice that the requisite 449 exclusive NDPS courts be established at the earliest,” the Court recorded. The bench directed all States and Union Territories to urgently arrange the necessary court infrastructure and appoint judicial and administrative staff to bridge the deficit. The order came in the Supreme Court’s ongoing suo motu proceedings initiated to expedite trials under special statutes, including the NDPS Act, the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), and the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act. The Court had previously instructed authorities to assess requirements to conduct these trials on a day-to-day basis and conclude them within one year. She added that operational courts have increased from 113 to 176. ASG Bhati also presented an update on exclusive NIA courts, noting that eight new courts have been added, bringing the national tally to 22. During the hearing, Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya took strong exception to the State government lodging multiple FIRs against the TMC leader and indicated that the Court may consider barring registration of any further FIRs against Banerjee without its permission, if complaints against him continue to be filed in similar manner. "Why was the whistle not blown one year back? Every day issues coming one after another based on one complaint and another. If this thing goes on, then I am telling you that I am going to pass an order for blanket injunction," said Justice Bhattacharyya. The Court noted that the repeated registration of cases was becoming a matter of concern. "Enough is enough. From May 2026. I am hearing these matters. The Court was referring to an earlier order passed by a coordinate bench in proceedings involving West Bengal BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, under which further FIRs against him could not be registered without the court's permission. items.title: Kerala High Court asks trial court to reconsider Ansiba Hassan's plea for FIR against Lakshmi Priya
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday directed a trial court to reconsider Malayalam actress Ansiba Hassan's plea for the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against actress Lakshmi Priya and two representatives of an online media outlet, Can Channel Media [ Ansiba Hassan v State of Kerala & ors ]. The matter concerns a video circulated on social media of an interview given by Lakshmipriya to Can Channel. Hassan claims that the interview included sexually coloured remarks against her, which were intended to outrage her modesty and damage her reputation. She asserted that Lakshmipriya's comments and the circulation of such content disclosed the commission of cognisable criminal offences. However, on July 27, an Ernakulam Judicial First Class Magistrate dismissed her plea to order the registration of an FIR into the matter. Hassan had challenged this order before the High Court. Today, Justice Jobin Sebastian ordered the trial court to reconsider the matter. " Accordingly, the Crl MC is allowed in part, and Annexure 7 order is set aside . The matter is remitted to the learned Magistrate for fresh consideration. The Magistrate shall independently examine the allegations contained in the complaint and the material available on record and determine, in accordance with law, whether the allegations prima facie disclose commission of a cognisable offence and, if so, whether the circumstances warrant a direction for police investigation. The learned magistrate shall also consider whether police investigation is necessary for the purpose of collection of evidence which cannot be effectively secured by the complainant herself," the High Court ordered. Justice Jobin Sebastian The case arose from an interview given by Lakshmi Priya to Can Channel Media, amid an ongoing feud between Lakshmi Priya and Hassan. Hassan filed a complaint against Lakshmi Priya, Can Channel Media owner Sukumar and interviewer Suresh in her complaint, alleging that they portrayed her as 'a woman of immoral character' and thereby committed offences under Sections 75 (iv) (sexual harassment) and 79 (outraging modesty of woman) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS). items.title: Noida workers' protest: Allahabad High Court quashes NSA detention of DU grad Akriti Chaudhary
items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Tuesday quashed the preventive detention of Akriti Chaudhary, a History graduate from Delhi University, under the National Security Act (NSA) [Akriti Chaudhary (Detenue) v Union of India and Others] The order was passed by a Bench of Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev on a habeas corpus petition challenging Chaudhary's detention. "The continued incarceration of the petitioner under the provisions of the NSA is violative of her rights under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. The order of detention along with the grounds of detention, being devoid of any material warranting the incarceration of the Petitioner under the NSA and the impugned order having been passed without application of mind, are quashed," the Court said. Justice Atul Sreedharan and Justice Achal Sachdev The development was confirmed to the Bar & Bench by Advocate Charlie Prakash who said that the Court has also directed the Noida authorities to pay a compensation of ₹5 lakh to Chaudhary. Senior Advocate Colin Gonsalves, along with advocate Prakash, represented Chaudhary in the case. Chaudhary will continue to remain in custody as she is yet to secure bail in various cases registered in connection with the industrial workers' protest that took place in Noida in April. The workers had staged protests to demand better wages and working conditions. The protests had also turned violent, leading to police action against the workers. Chaudhary had attended a demonstration to express solidarity with the workers. The police accused her of playing a major role in the violence during the workers' protest. In her petition challenging the detention, Chaudhary said that she had participated in the agitation in her capacity as a social worker and was not an organizer of the protests. “The allegations contained in the grounds of detention are vague, omnibus, general in nature and devoid of material particulars,” the plea added. items.title: Kochi filmmaker is only Indian to be selected to Artists Academy, New York Film Festival
items.summary: In the list of roles Raymond George Dias has played in his young life – filmmaker, photographer, and multidisciplinary artist, with a background in law – you might look for the word ‘poet’, if you have come across one or many of his works. His words and visuals tend to carry the hangover of a poem, lyrical and musical pieces hopping through time and space. All that art has paved the way for his selection in the Film at Lincoln Center (FLC) Artists Academy 2026, held as part of the New York Film Festival. He is one of the 12 filmmakers from around the world to participate in the programme, to be held between September 25 and October 12. The FLC Academies support the next generation of film artists and critics by conducting a workshop, during which participants can meet with established filmmakers and others, and find new opportunities. The FLC page describes Raymond’s approach to art as a “spiritual rite, a pilgrimage of unmaking and becoming”. “I am the only filmmaker selected from India. For me, it feels particularly meaningful because the programme brings together emerging filmmakers with established artists and people working across the international film community at a moment when I'm beginning to develop my first feature,” says Raymond, who hails from Kochi. From Raymond's documentary 'Lonely Miracle in the River of Time' The young filmmaker’s journey is as interesting as the randomness of his art. He studied law at National University of Advanced Legal Studies (NUALS) in Kochi, completed a Master’s degree in Law at the University of Auckland in New Zealand, and somewhere along the way, slipped into the world of cinema. "I practised law for a while, but alongside it I had always been drawn towards creating through different means of expression I picked up along the way, from photography to writing, music, collage, and eventually film," he explains. items.title: What are the Sarkaria report and ED document Vijay cited to accuse the DMK of corruption?
items.summary: The Sarkaria Commission report of the 1970s is back in the spotlight in the DMK corruption debate in Tamil Nadu. For years, former Chief Minister and AIADMK supremo J Jayalalithaa had used the Commission’s findings to attack the DMK both in the Assembly and in her political speeches. Years later, the current Chief Minister, C Joseph Vijay, used the same report to launch a broad attack on the DMK, citing allegations of corruption during its previous tenures. The Sarkaria Commission was a one-man commission appointed in 1976 to investigate allegations of corruption and misuse of power against the DMK government that was in power in Tamil Nadu from 1971-1976. M Karunanidhi had been the Chief Minister then and many of the allegations that the Commission looked at were directly related to him. It was convened after Dravidian stalwart MG Ramachandran submitted complaints to the President, after he broke away from the DMK, alleging corruption involving Karunanidhi and his ministers. After the DMK government was dismissed on January 31, 1976, during the Emergency, Justice Ranjit Singh Sarkaria, a Supreme Court judge, was appointed to head the inquiry. The Commission was asked to examine 28 allegations, covering alleged corruption, misuse of official position and irregularities involving the Karunanidhi government. Vijay alleged that the Sarkaria Commission had recorded an instance in which a relative of Karunanidhi had demanded a 2.5% commission in connection with the award of a tender. He also alleged that the report had recorded that Karunanidhi had misused his office to facilitate the award of the Veeranam water tender to the Sathyanarayana Brothers group and had pressured then Chief Engineer Hussain. The Veeranam project was supposed to provide drinking water to the city of Chennai, which faced acute water scarcity then. In 1970, the company was awarded the contract to manufacture, supply, lay, and test pre-stressed concrete pipes. The project came to a halt after allegations of corruption and the subsequent Sarkaria Commission inquiry. Though the Commission had looked at 28 allegations, the report, however, concluded on only seven allegations, finding six of them to be true or partially true and one to be false. However, no findings were published on the Veeranam project. Veeranam was the tenth allegation that the commission probed.
